title: Introduction to Artifacts
description: Understand what Claude Artifacts are, how they work, and why they transform Claude from a text tool into an interactive creation platform.

data.text: Artifacts are Claude's most distinctive feature. When Claude generates an Artifact, it produces a self-contained piece of content — code, a document, a visualization, or a web component — that appears in a separate panel alongside the chat. You can view, edit, and sometimes run the artifact directly. This transforms Claude from a text-based assistant into a lightweight creation and prototyping environment.
How Artifacts Differ from Regular Responses

A regular Claude response is text in the chat. An Artifact is a structured, standalone object. Think of it like the difference between someone describing a drawing and someone handing you the actual drawing. Artifacts can be HTML pages, Python scripts, React components, SVG diagrams, data visualizations, or formatted documents.

cards.title: Regular Chat Response
cards.description: Text-only output in the conversation stream.

cards.title: Claude Artifact
cards.description: A self-contained, interactive piece of content rendered in a separate panel.
cons: Complex artifacts may have rendering limits

data.title: Common artifact types:
items: Web pages — HTML/CSS/JS that render interactive content
Code files — Python scripts, React components, data analysis scripts
Documents — Formatted reports, markdown documents, structured outlines
Visualizations — SVG diagrams, charts, data plots

data.text: Claude does not generate Artifacts automatically — you need to ask for them. The simplest way is to include 'as an artifact' or 'in an artifact' in your prompt. You can also be specific about the type: 'Create an interactive HTML artifact that...' or 'Write a Python script as an artifact that...'

data.title: Artifact request examples
data.content:
Web page: 'Create an HTML artifact for a personal landing page with a hero section, about section, and contact form.'

Python script: 'Write a Python script as an artifact that analyzes a CSV file and generates a summary report with charts.'

SVG diagram: 'Create an SVG artifact showing the architecture of a typical web application.'

data.text: One of the most powerful aspects of Artifacts is the iteration cycle. You can ask Claude to modify an existing artifact — change colors, add features, fix bugs, or completely rebuild it. Claude has access to the previous artifact in the conversation context, so each iteration builds on the last.

data.title: Iterate in small steps
data.text: When iterating on an artifact, make small, specific requests. 'Change the header color to blue' is more effective than 'make it look better'. Claude will keep a coherent artifact across many iterations, but the more specific your feedback, the better the result.

You do not need to know how to code to use Artifacts. You can ask Claude to create an artifact for you, then use the rendered output directly. For example, ask for an HTML invoice template, a project timeline visualization, or a simple web calculator — Claude builds it, and you use the result. The ability to make small tweaks (like changing colors or text) without coding knowledge makes Artifacts accessible to everyone.

data.title: Artifacts essentials
points: Artifacts are interactive, standalone pieces of content generated alongside chat
Ask for them by including 'as an artifact' in your prompt
Types include web pages, code, documents, and visualizations
Iterate by asking Claude to modify the existing artifact
No coding skills required — ask Claude to build, then use or refine the output
